title: Welder
what_it_is: Joins steel to a written procedure. On a yard that is plate, sections and structures; on pipe it is spools and tie-ins, often in positions where the pipe cannot be turned. The qualification is not a general licence — it covers one process, one position range, one material group and one thickness range, and a welder outside that range is unqualified however experienced.

certificates.levels: By process, position, material and thickness range
certificates.who_requires_it: Every European yard and offshore client. Usually needs a six-monthly employer endorsement to stay valid.
US-influenced and oil & gas fabrication scopes.
Norwegian Continental Shelf work.

codes.means: Pipe fixed at 45°, cannot be turned. The hardest standard position; usually covers the easier ones.
Pipe fixed horizontally — vertical and overhead welding, no tilt.
Vertical up. Slow and controlled; most structural work asks for it.
Vertical down. Faster, thinner material; not a substitute for PF.
TIG — root runs on pipe, stainless and duplex.
MMA / stick — portable, wind-tolerant, common offshore.
Flux-cored MAG — heavy structural deposition.

check_on_cv: Which process numbers, and does the certificate range cover the work you are placing them on
Position: 6G and 5G are pipe; PF and PC are plate and structure
Material group — carbon steel does not qualify anyone for duplex or aluminium
Thickness range printed on the certificate
Date of the last employer endorsement, not just the issue date
Whether the test was witnessed by a third party, and which
red_flags: "All positions, all processes" with no certificate numbers
A certificate more than six months old with no endorsement
Duplex or super duplex claimed with a carbon steel qualification
Years of experience given instead of a qualification range

questions.q: Which processes and positions are you certified in right now, to which standard, and what thickness and material range does the certificate cover?
questions.good_answer: Names the process numbers, the position, the standard and the range without hesitating — e.g. 141 and 111, 6G, EN ISO 9606-1, carbon steel 8–20 mm — and offers to send the certificate.

questions.q: When was your qualification last endorsed, and by whom?
questions.good_answer: Gives a date inside the last six months and names the employer or test house that signed it.

questions.q: Talk me through a root run on 6G pipe: what do you set, and what goes wrong?
questions.good_answer: Describes purge, gap and land, heat input, and the failure they watch for — lack of fusion at the 6 o'clock, or oxidation from a lost purge.

questions.q: Have you welded duplex or stainless, and what changes?
questions.good_answer: Talks about heat input control and interpass temperature rather than saying it is the same as carbon steel.

questions.q: What NDT has been applied to your welds, and have you had repairs?
questions.good_answer: Knows their repair rate, does not claim zero, and can say what the defect was and what they changed.

title: Pipefitter
what_it_is: Takes an isometric drawing and turns it into pipework: measures, cuts, bevels, fits and aligns spools ready for the welder, then bolts up flanges to torque. On offshore modifications the fitting is the slow part — the welding is quick once the fit-up is right.

certificates.levels: National — e.g. Norwegian fagbrev, Danish svendebrev
certificates.who_requires_it: Nordic yards often ask for the national trade certificate by name.
Most offshore operators before anyone breaks or makes a joint.

codes.means: Isometric drawing — the single-line pipe drawing a fitter works from.
A prefabricated length of pipe with its fittings, made in the shop and installed as one piece.
The joint connecting new pipework to an existing live system. Usually the permit-heavy part.
Cutting, grinding or welding — needs a permit and often a fire watch.

check_on_cv: Can they read isometrics — ask, do not assume
Whether the experience is shop spooling or site tie-ins; they are different jobs
Flange management or torque certification, and when it expires
Which materials: carbon, stainless, duplex, GRE
Whether they have worked to a permit system offshore
red_flags: "Pipefitter/welder" with no welding qualification and no fitting detail
Only shop experience offered for a live tie-in scope
No mention of drawings anywhere in the CV

questions.q: Walk me through fitting a spool from the isometric to the point the welder starts.
questions.good_answer: Describes reading the iso, marking, cutting and bevelling, checking gap and alignment, and tacking — in that order, with tolerances.

questions.q: How do you set root gap and alignment on a butt joint, and what tools do you use?
questions.good_answer: Names hi-lo gauge, wraparound, levels; gives a gap in millimetres consistent with the process.

questions.q: Have you done tie-ins on a live system, and what does the permit process look like?
questions.good_answer: Talks about isolation, permit, gas testing and the standby, not just the mechanical work.

questions.q: Do you hold flange-management or torque-bolting certification, and when does it expire?
questions.good_answer: Names the scheme and a date, and offers the certificate.

questions.q: What is the difference in fitting stainless or duplex compared with carbon steel?
questions.good_answer: Mentions separate tooling and avoiding carbon contamination rather than saying there is no difference.

title: Blaster
what_it_is: Prepares steel so a coating will hold: abrasive blasting to a cleanliness grade and a surface profile, then keeping the surface clean until the painter reaches it. The whole coating system depends on this being right, and it cannot be inspected once painted over.

certificates.levels: Inspector I–III — for inspecting, not for blasting
certificates.who_requires_it: Norwegian and North Sea work where inspection is required.
International and oil & gas coating scopes.

codes.means: Near-white blast to ISO 8501-1 — the usual offshore requirement.
White metal — the highest grade.
The roughness left by the abrasive, measured in microns. Too smooth and the coating fails to key.
Contamination measured before coating; over the limit and the surface must be washed and reblasted.

check_on_cv: Which cleanliness grades they have worked to, by standard
Whether they have worked in a cabinet, in a yard, or on site with containment
Experience with soluble salt testing and dew point control
Confined space training if the work is tanks or ballast compartments
red_flags: Grades quoted without a standard
No mention of dew point or humidity anywhere
Blasting and painting used interchangeably in the CV

questions.q: What cleanliness grade and surface profile do you normally work to, and how is each checked?
questions.good_answer: Names Sa 2.5 to ISO 8501-1, a profile in microns, and describes visual comparators and a profile gauge or tape.

questions.q: What conditions stop you blasting or coating?
questions.good_answer: Talks about steel temperature against dew point, relative humidity, and waiting rather than proceeding.

questions.q: How do you handle soluble salts?
questions.good_answer: Describes testing, the limit, and washing and reblasting when it fails.

questions.q: Have you worked in confined spaces, and what changes?
questions.good_answer: Mentions permit, ventilation, standby man and air-fed breathing equipment.

questions.q: What happens if the coating goes on over a surface that has flash-rusted?
questions.good_answer: Says it fails and has to be reblasted, rather than treating it as acceptable.

title: Industrial painter
what_it_is: Applies coating systems to specification: primer, intermediate and topcoat, each to a thickness range, in conditions the specification allows. Usually airless spray, sometimes brush and roller for stripe coats on edges and welds.

certificates.who_requires_it: Where inspection sign-off is required — the applicator may work under an inspector rather than hold it.
International coating scopes.

codes.means: Dry film thickness in microns — what gets measured and signed off.
Wet film thickness — checked with a comb during application.
An extra brush coat on edges, welds and bolts, where spray goes thin.
The Norwegian coating standard; its systems are referenced by number.

check_on_cv: Which coating systems and standards, by name
Airless spray experience and the equipment used
Whether they do stripe coats — its absence tells you a lot
Offshore or yard, and whether under containment
red_flags: "Painter" with only decorating or marine topside cosmetic work
No thickness figures anywhere in the CV
Cannot name a coating manufacturer or system

questions.q: Which coating systems have you applied, and to what standard?
questions.good_answer: Names a standard such as NORSOK M-501, a manufacturer, and a system with coats and thicknesses.

questions.q: How do you control and check film thickness?
questions.good_answer: WFT comb during application, DFT gauge after cure, and knows the specified range and what happens outside it.

questions.q: When do you apply a stripe coat and why?
questions.good_answer: Edges, welds, bolts and corners, because sprayed film thins there and those are where failure starts.

questions.q: What conditions would stop you spraying?
questions.good_answer: Dew point margin, humidity, wind and overspray risk — and says they stop rather than continue.

questions.q: What is the recoat window, and what if you miss it?
questions.good_answer: Knows it varies by product, and that overrunning means sweeping or abrading for adhesion.

title: NDT technician
what_it_is: Checks welds and materials without cutting them, and writes what they found. The level matters: a level 2 performs and reports to a written procedure, a level 3 writes the procedure and carries technical responsibility for the method.

certificates.who_requires_it: UK and much of the North Sea.
The international standard PCN and others certify to.
Weld inspection rather than NDT method work.

codes.means: Ultrasonic testing — internal flaws.
Phased array UT — steered beam, cross-sectional image; often replaces radiography.
Time of flight diffraction — accurate flaw sizing, usually paired with PAUT.
Magnetic particle — surface cracks in ferrous material.
Dye penetrant — surface-breaking cracks, any material.
Radiography — needs exclusion zones, so often night work.

check_on_cv: Which methods, at which level, and the expiry of each — they expire separately
Whether the certificate is PCN, ISO 9712 or an employer scheme
Vision test date, which lapses more often than people expect
PAUT and TOFD experience specifically, if the scope needs them
red_flags: "NDT Level 2" with no methods named
One expiry date offered for several methods
Radiography claimed with no mention of source handling or exclusion zones

questions.q: Which methods are you certified in, at what level, under which scheme, and when does each expire?
questions.good_answer: Lists them separately with dates — e.g. UT level 2 PCN to March 2028, MT and PT level 2 to a different date.

questions.q: When was your last vision test?
questions.good_answer: Gives a date within the last twelve months and knows it is a requirement.

questions.q: Talk me through setting up for a PAUT scan on a butt weld.
questions.good_answer: Calibration blocks, wedge and probe choice, scan plan, encoder setup, and reference sensitivity.

questions.q: How do you report a defect you are not certain about?
questions.good_answer: Records what was seen, refers to the acceptance criteria and escalates to level 3 rather than deciding alone.

questions.q: Which acceptance standard do you usually work to?
questions.good_answer: Names one — ISO 5817, ASME VIII, a client spec — rather than saying 'the client's'.

title: Scaffolder
what_it_is: Builds the access everyone else works from, and signs it off. Offshore it is often suspended or hanging scaffold in awkward geometry, under a permit, with a load and a wind case that matter.

certificates.who_requires_it: UK sites almost without exception.

certificates.levels: e.g. Norwegian stillasbygger course by height class
certificates.who_requires_it: Norwegian and Danish sites, by the height they are certified to.

codes.means: The tag on a scaffold saying who inspected it and when. No tag, no access.
Suspended from structure rather than built from the ground — common offshore.
The formal sign-off transferring a completed scaffold to the trades using it.

check_on_cv: Card level and expiry, and whether it is CISRS or a national scheme
The height class they are certified to, in Nordic schemes
Offshore or onshore, and suspended experience specifically
Whether they have inspected and tagged, not only built
red_flags: Card claimed but no number or expiry
"Scaffolder" with only labouring or dismantling experience
No mention of inspection or tagging for a supervisor role

questions.q: Which card do you hold, at what level, and when does it expire?
questions.good_answer: Names the scheme, the grade and a date, and can give the card number.

questions.q: Have you built suspended or hanging scaffold offshore?
questions.good_answer: Describes the anchoring, the load case and the permit, not just that they have done it.

questions.q: Who may tag a scaffold, and what does the tag mean to someone using it?
questions.good_answer: Only a competent inspector; the tag says it has been checked and is safe to use, with a date.

questions.q: What do you do if you are asked to modify someone else's scaffold?
questions.good_answer: Does not modify without authorisation, removes or changes the tag, and re-inspects.

questions.q: What stops work at height on a given day?
questions.good_answer: Wind speed against the limit, ice, lightning — and names the limit.

title: Rope access technician
what_it_is: Reaches work that scaffolding cannot economically reach — blades, splash zones, flare tips, confined structures — using two independent ropes. The trade underneath matters as much as the rope skill: a level 1 who is also a welder is worth more than a level 1 alone.

certificates.levels: 1, 2, 3 — a level 3 must be on site to supervise and hold the rescue plan
certificates.who_requires_it: European offshore and wind work, nearly universally.
North America; not always accepted in Europe — check with the client.
Wind sites, alongside IRATA.

codes.means: The supervisor who runs the team and the rescue plan. No level 3, no rope team.
The written plan for getting a casualty off the rope. Required before anyone goes over the edge.
The record of hours on rope, needed for revalidation and often asked for by clients.

check_on_cv: IRATA level and expiry — three years, and revalidation needs logged hours
The trade underneath the rope: welding, NDT, coating, blade repair
Logged hours, and whether the logbook is up to date
Offshore medical and safety training, which rope access does not replace
red_flags: IRATA claimed with no level or number
Rope access as the only skill for a scope that needs a trade
A lapsed certificate offered as current

questions.q: What IRATA level do you hold, what is your number, and when does it expire?
questions.good_answer: Gives level, number and date, and knows revalidation is three-yearly with logged hours.

questions.q: How many hours are in your logbook, and when did you last log?
questions.good_answer: Gives a figure and a recent date rather than a vague answer.

questions.q: What trade do you do on the rope?
questions.good_answer: Names it and can talk about it in the same detail as a ground-based tradesman.

questions.q: Who writes the rescue plan and what is in it?
questions.good_answer: The level 3 supervisor; describes casualty recovery and that it exists before work starts.

questions.q: What would stop you going on the rope?
questions.good_answer: Wind, lightning, sea state, no level 3 on site, or damaged equipment — and says they refuse.

title: Wind turbine technician
what_it_is: Installs, commissions and maintains turbines — mechanical, electrical and hydraulic work inside a nacelle or up a tower, offshore often on a 2:2 rotation. Safety training is the entry ticket and is checked in a database before anyone travels.

certificates.levels: First aid, manual handling, fire awareness, working at heights; sea survival offshore
certificates.who_requires_it: Every wind client. Recorded in WINDA and checked by ID.

certificates.levels: Basic Technical Training — mechanical, electrical, hydraulic
certificates.who_requires_it: Often asked for alongside BST for technician roles.
Offshore wind.

codes.means: The GWO training database. A WINDA ID is how a client verifies the training.
The housing at the top of the tower containing the drivetrain.
Bringing a turbine into service after installation — testing and sign-off.
Two weeks on, two off — the common offshore rotation.

check_on_cv: A WINDA ID, not just the words "GWO trained"
Which GWO modules and their expiry — two years for most
Whether the experience is installation, commissioning or service; they are different
Electrical qualification if the role is E&I rather than mechanical
red_flags: "GWO certified" with no WINDA ID and no modules named
Onshore-only experience offered for an offshore rotation
No offshore medical for an offshore role

questions.q: What is your WINDA ID, which GWO modules do you hold and when do they expire?
questions.good_answer: Gives the ID, lists the modules and gives dates — and knows sea survival is separate.

questions.q: Is your experience installation, commissioning or service?
questions.good_answer: Says which, and describes the work in terms specific to it.

questions.q: Which turbine platforms have you worked on?
questions.good_answer: Names manufacturers and models rather than saying 'all of them'.

questions.q: What is your offshore medical status and when does it expire?
questions.good_answer: Names the type and a date, and knows it is required to travel.

questions.q: Describe a fault you diagnosed in a nacelle and how you found it.
questions.good_answer: Walks through the symptom, what they checked and what it turned out to be, using the right terms.

title: Electrician
what_it_is: Installs, terminates and tests electrical systems — cable pulling, glanding and termination, panels, instrumentation, and testing before energising. Offshore and in hazardous areas the Ex qualification is a separate thing from being an electrician.

certificates.levels: e.g. Norwegian fagbrev elektriker, Danish elektriker
certificates.who_requires_it: Nordic sites, by name. Note the authorisation itself usually sits with the employing company, not the individual.
Hazardous areas: oil & gas, chemical, some offshore wind.
Benelux sites.

codes.means: Equipment and practice for explosive atmospheres. A separate qualification from the trade.
Terminating a cable into equipment with the correct gland and seal — the part Ex inspection scrutinises.
Electrical and Instrumentation, usually treated as one discipline offshore.
Low and high voltage. HV needs separate authorisation and switching competence.

check_on_cv: The national trade certificate, and which country issued it
Ex/ATEX units held and expiry, separately from the trade certificate
LV or HV, and whether they have switching authorisation
Instrumentation experience if the role is E&I
Whether they have worked to a permit system
red_flags: "Ex certified" with no scheme or units named
HV claimed with no switching authorisation
Domestic or commercial installation experience offered for industrial work

questions.q: Which trade certificate do you hold and from which country?
questions.good_answer: Names it precisely and can produce it; understands that authorisation may sit with the employer.

questions.q: Do you hold Ex or ATEX certification — which units, and when do they expire?
questions.good_answer: Names the scheme and units rather than saying 'yes, Ex'.

questions.q: Talk me through glanding a cable into an Ex e enclosure.
questions.good_answer: Describes gland selection, sealing, thread engagement and what an inspector would fail it for.

questions.q: Have you worked LV or HV, and do you hold switching authorisation?
questions.good_answer: Is clear about which, and does not claim HV switching without authorisation.

questions.q: What testing do you do before energising?
questions.good_answer: Continuity, insulation resistance, polarity and earth checks, and records them.

title: Mechanical fitter
what_it_is: Installs, aligns, maintains and overhauls rotating and static mechanical equipment — pumps, gearboxes, valves, hydraulics — and takes it apart and back together on shutdowns. On a yard it is also structural fitting: plate, sections and assemblies made ready for welding.

certificates.levels: e.g. Norwegian fagbrev industrimekaniker, Danish industrimekaniker
certificates.who_requires_it: Nordic yards and industrial sites.
Offshore operators, before breaking or making joints.
Anywhere loads are moved, which is most of the job.

codes.means: Setting two shafts true, usually with dial gauges or laser. The measurable part of the job.
A planned stop for work that cannot be done running. Short, intense, and where fitters earn their money.
Bolt tightening to a specified figure and sequence — recorded and signed.

check_on_cv: Rotating equipment or structural fitting — they are different trades in practice
Which equipment types and manufacturers
Alignment method: dial gauge, laser, or 'by eye'
Torque and flange-management certification
Shutdown and turnaround experience specifically
red_flags: "Mechanic" with only automotive experience
Alignment described without any measurement
No mention of drawings or torque figures

questions.q: Is your experience rotating equipment, structural fitting, or both?
questions.good_answer: Says which and gives examples with equipment types or structures.

questions.q: How do you align a pump and motor, and what tolerance do you work to?
questions.good_answer: Names dial indicators or laser, describes soft foot checks, and gives a tolerance figure.

questions.q: Do you hold torque or flange-management certification?
questions.good_answer: Names the scheme and expiry, and describes the sequence and recording.

questions.q: Describe a shutdown you worked and what your scope was.
questions.good_answer: Gives the plant, the duration, the specific equipment and what went wrong.

questions.q: What rigging and lifting are you certified for?
questions.good_answer: Names the certificate and is clear about what they may and may not sling.
